messages:
perf-bot: Nightdash alert: latency deviation detected for rc-2026.03.15 on model-x86-small (p95 +38%, p50 +14%). Threshold breached at 03:12 UTC.

maya: saw this on the dashboard. p95 jump correlates with the 03:00 deploy window.

leo: which merge landed around 03:00?

priya: looks like #4123 (kernel-routing: small-window batching tweak) merged at 02:58 by @sam.

sam: yep, that wasm/kernel-selector change tightened the batching window from 8ms -> 4ms for streaming workloads to reduce tail in steady state.

alex: pinging perf infra: CI perf-run for rc-2026.03.15 failed one benchmark earlier (throughput_drop_kernel_selector). I didn't see a blocker in CI because it was flaky before.

maya: can we bisect quickly? if it's #4123 we should hold the rollout.

leo: starting a local bisect against last-green commit + current HEAD.

leo: git bisect start --term-old="good" --term-new="bad"\ngit bisect good origin/rc-2026.03.14\ngit bisect bad HEAD

leo: first bad commit reported: 7a2f4d3 (PR #4123).

priya: oof. that was the one that changed continuous batching heuristic + kernel preference logic.

sam: note: the change was intended to reduce latency by shrinking the wait window; might be increasing per-token overhead because it forces kernel handoffs more frequently.

maya: can we get a quick flamegraph of the p95 path? I ran a perf sample on a repro run (100 concurrent streams, seq_len=1024) and attached a trace: http://intra.example.com/perf/traces/1719987654/fg.svg

alex: I see increased time in kernel_routing::choose_kernel and in kv_cache::refresh_hotset path. The routing change causes frequent cache misses and rebuilds for short prefixes.

priya: interesting — the small-window batching means we flush partial batches more often; KV cache prefetch logic expects slightly larger windows to amortize prefetch cost. When window shrinks, prefetches are evicted before reuse.

sam: can we try a quick patch to only apply the 4ms window for models > 2B params and keep 8ms for small models?

leo: building a test branch now: revert the batching-window change for <=2B, keep the kernel-selector improvements.

leo: pushed branch: fix/batching-window-selective (diff: https://git.internal/r/12345)

maya: can we run that on the nightly perf harness? If green, we'll rollback the merged change or cherry-pick.

deploy-bot: Starting canary deploy of fix/batching-window-selective to rc-canary-3 (20% traffic).

perf-bot: Canary perf-run complete: p95 down -28% relative to bad HEAD, p50 neutral. Throughput restored to baseline.

priya: looks promising. I'd still like a longer run to confirm no throughput regressions at higher concurrency.

sam: agreed. schedule a 2-hour run on the perf board and keep the canary paused at 20%.

alex: recording this as a temporary rollback candidate: revert PR #4123 for small-models. We should follow up with a more nuanced kernel-handoff heuristic that avoids KV churn.

maya: @eng-runtime please add a post-deploy test that exercises kv-prefetch hotset reuse for small-window scenarios. We missed that in unit tests.

leo: adding an integration test to perf-harness: test_kv_hotset_reuse_small_window.

priya: also capture a trace for the failing run and attach to the PR for future debugging.

sam: noted. I’ll open a follow-up issue to iterate on kernel_selector so we don't need per-model heuristics.

maya: thanks team. holding the wider rollout for rc until perf-run overnight passes.

alex: filing a rollback PR and marking the release as blocked: https://git.internal/r/12346 (revert of #4123 for <=2B models).

perf-bot: Nightdash alert resolved for canary with fix/batching-window-selective. Monitor for 2 hours.

maya: closing triage for now, we'll reopen if the 2-hour run spikes. :thumbsup:
